sources: dossier=Net position line 12 ('Modes apply at the pending-to-stale transition ... never at node-run creation. Wait-set accumulation is a separate rule from queue/mode semantics') and Required behaviors line 23; doc=Boundaries line 19 said 'Owns: the per-mode rule applied at the walker's accumulate-or-queue gate ...'; code=cascade_walker.go never reads CascadeMode, all mode logic is applyCascadeModeRule at gate_evaluator.go:345 called from evaluateOneGate:82 before TransitionPendingToStale; test=scenario proofs (idempotent-mode-dedupes, sequenced-preserves-cascade-rounds) exercise the gate-evaluator path per dossier line 30.
note: Dossier transcript intent places all mode logic at the gate evaluator's pending-to-stale transition; the walker is mode-blind. The concept doc's Boundaries line and What-it-is paragraph misattributed mode behavior to the walker's accumulate-or-queue gate. Fixed the doc to own the rule solely at the gate-eval transition.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 24 ('Idempotency applies only when one or more stale rows sit in the queue ... with no stale, the run is always created ... idempotent-settled additionally compares against the most recent settled run'); doc=table idempotent-settled cell said 'compared against both the currently-queued stale and the most-recently-settled successful run ... if byte-equivalent to either'; code=gate_evaluator.go modeDropIfPriorEqual (373-394) checks priorStale first and only calls GetMostRecentSettledRun when priorStale is nil.
note: Dossier transcript intent (and the code, story, and decision it corroborates) establishes the settled-run comparison is a fallback used only when no prior cascade row exists, not a simultaneous both-checks comparison. Rewrote the idempotent-settled table cell to state the settled comparison fires only when no prior cascade row (pending or stale) exists.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12 ('Wait-set accumulation is a separate rule from queue/mode semantics') corroborating the Invariants-side reading; doc=What-it-is paragraph (line 11) said modes reshape 'how the walker's accumulate-or-queue gate ... interacts with subsequent rounds', contradicting Invariants line 37 ('The mode does not change the per-sender-node accumulation rule'); code=cascade_walker.go carries no mode branch, confirming the Invariants side.
note: The doc contradicted itself between the opening paragraph and its own Invariants section; dossier intent and code both side with the Invariants reading (mode never touches walker accumulation). Rewrote the What-it-is paragraph to remove the walker-mode-branch implication and align with line 37.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12 ('Modes apply at the pending-to-stale transition — the moment the attribute bag is resolved'); doc=most-recent row's gate-eval cell said 'the surviving stale transitions on its own wait-set draining'; code=evaluateOneGate (gate_evaluator.go:50-102) evaluates pending rows and calls TransitionPendingToStale on wait-set drain — the transition is pending-to-stale, not a stale-row transition.
note: The doc's phrasing inverted the state machine: it is the pending row that transitions to stale on wait-set drain, not a stale row transitioning on its own draining. Fixed by restructuring the table around a single 'behavior at the gate evaluator's pending->stale transition' column, removing the inverted phrase entirely.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 32 ('idempotent comparison resolves a still-pending prior peer's bag on demand' — one of the four ratified gate fixes, 2026-07-05, transcript); doc=idempotent rows said comparison target is 'the currently-queued stale row'; code=GetPriorCascadeStaleNotClaimed (postgres/nodes.go:902) filters state IN ('pending','stale'), and bagsEqual (gate_evaluator.go:398-425) carries an on-demand-resolve fallback for pending priors lacking a persisted bag.
note: Dossier transcript intent explicitly ratifies on-demand resolution of a still-pending prior peer's bag as a root fix, confirming the doc understated the comparison set (stale-only) versus the actual pending-or-stale set. Rewrote the idempotent-queue/idempotent-settled cells to say 'the most recent prior cascade row (pending or stale, whichever has the highest sequence)'.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 24 ('comparing against the most recent stale's bag' — singular, most-recent, not queue-wide); doc=idempotent rows said 'the currently-queued stale row' with definite article, obscuring that multiple queued rows can coexist; code=GetPriorCascadeStaleNotClaimed (postgres/nodes.go:903-912) is ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 1, i.e. consecutive-duplicate suppression against only the highest-sequence prior.
note: Dossier's own phrase 'the most recent stale's bag' matches the code's highest-sequence-only comparison, corroborating that the finding's queue-wide misreading risk is real given the doc's ambiguous singular phrasing. Rewrote the cells to explicitly say 'the most recent prior cascade row ... whichever has the highest sequence', making the consecutive-only semantics unambiguous.
